Alternative Low-Tech Cooling Strategies Used in Arid Environments
If your goal is passive temperature control in Slab City without digging a full subterranean bunker, alternative earth-integrated and passive cooling designs are often more viable:
Earth Berming (Semi-Underground): Rather than digging down, build at ground level and pile earth high against the north, east, and west walls. This provides high thermal mass while preventing floodwaters from flowing inside.
Earthships / Earthbag Construction: Utilizing stacked soil-filled tires or sandbags covered in thick plaster creates dense thermal mass walls above ground that absorb heat during the day and release it at night.
Sub-Surface "Cold Pits" or Dugouts: A shallow pit (3–4 feet deep) covered by a high, shaded roof with wide open airflow reduces radiant heat while lowering flood risks compared to a deep basement.
Shade Canopies & Double Roofing: Creating a secondary canopy roof over a living space blocks direct sunlight completely, allowing wind to carry away radiant heat before it reaches the structure.
